paragraphs: This occupation provides clinical and surgical care for diseases, injuries and defects of oral and maxillofacial hard and soft tissues, working with anesthesia, orthodontic and prosthodontic teams. History, examinations, imaging, plans, consent and follow-up records form a chain of responsibility. Material record conflicts or omissions need timely verification and handover under institutional procedures. Qualified teams must address emergencies promptly; incomplete paperwork is not a universal instruction to stop all care.

Core process: Check symptoms, oral and maxillofacial imaging, and systemic risks; identify impacted teeth, infection, tumors, or trauma; determine the surgical scope, anesthesia, and consultation plan; explain alternatives, risks, and recovery.
Works in hospitals, dental specialty clinics, or surgical centers, and may take on acute maxillofacial trauma and infection.
Common tools and systems: dental imaging, CT, oral surgery instruments, anesthesia monitoring equipment, and electronic medical records.

U.S. general dentists also require professional dental education and state licensure; oral and maxillofacial surgery involves additional specialty surgical training. Check mainland China dental education, physician qualifications, registration and post requirements separately; a U.S. DDS/DMD or board certification does not directly grant Chinese authority.
Qualified delivery must demonstrate: imaging diagnosis, surgical plans, anesthesia assessment, informed consent, surgery, and follow-up records.
U.S. occupational scope and Chinese position titles or credentials need not correspond one-to-one; local requirements are verified by region and employer.
General dentistry and OMS both involve professional education and licensing. Compare specialty training, tasks and authority, rather than claiming general dentists do not perform surgery.
These comparisons use each U.S. O*NET task definition and establish neither credential equivalence nor direct transfer eligibility.

Orthodontics focuses on dentofacial correction and prosthodontics on function and prostheses. Dental assistants and technicians undertake limited assistance and fabrication respectively. Pediatric surgery involves different populations and medical training.
General dentists also need professional dental education and licensing; OMS adds specialty surgical training, rather than a simple surgery/no-surgery distinction.
Compare your interest in broad dental care and specialty surgery.
Explorer
Trial field comparison with the complete fictional K01/L01-v1 text records, checking every output against its source value; do not interpret images, diagnose disease or decide surgery.
Incumbent
Check imaging diagnosis, surgical plans, anesthesia assessment, informed consent, surgery, and follow-up records, and observe authorization.
Team lead
Check tool use, clinical review, and the responsibility for surgery, anesthesia, and anomaly escalation; document organization does not change medical authority.
Career changer
Compare the education, training, and authority of the target dental, pediatric surgery, or technical position; oral and maxillofacial surgical authority cannot be transferred.

A comparable nationwide occupational median, percentiles and uniform starting pay remain unavailable. In 2025, urban non-private and private health and social work averages were 146,266 and 75,631 yuan per year before tax, measured separately. The industry includes multiple occupations; these are not OMS wages, an individual range or owner-operated clinic profits. The survey covers urban legal entities with five or more workers under the respective non-private/private survey methods, excluding individual businesses and freelancers outside unit employment.
Chinese positions require separate verification of region, employer, duties, shift system, and qualifications; the U.S. 29-1022.00 annual salary cannot be directly converted.
Insufficient evidence: China-wide wage percentiles and unified starting pay for this occupation are missing, and broad industry averages are not used as substitutes.

Verification note: oral and maxillofacial surgery, anesthesia, informed consent, and complication management must be verified against Chinese statutory qualifications and organizational authority; U.S. dental training, licensure, and industry wages do not grant Chinese surgical or anesthesia authority.
The BLS precise occupation 29-1022.00 had a 2025 median annual wage of 352,220 U.S. dollars; statistical distributions do not represent individual contracts.
Wage percentiles should follow the official details for the same occupation; percentiles from parent groups or adjacent occupations must not be carried over.
Region, industry, shift system, hours, experience, and qualifications can change actual offers.
In 2025, about 5600 people were employed in the United States, with the statistical scope being 29-1022.00.

For exact U.S. occupation 29-1022, projected employment growth for 2025–2035 is 5.6%, with an official net increase of 300 over the decade. The 200 annual average openings include replacements; they are neither the decade’s net increase nor current vacancies. Aggregate projections establish no AI adoption, technology displacement or individual unemployment.
U.S. wages and projections cannot replace Chinese wages or individual hiring probability.

The following are occupational risk scenarios and cannot be used as guidance for diagnosis, surgery, or anesthesia practice; they should be handled according to local scope of practice and organizational procedures.

Explore the context of infection, breathing or swallowing difficulty, and nerve injury or bleeding after wisdom-tooth removal, alongside team communication and handover. The cards distinguish specific source contexts from editorial questions, without ranking or incidence estimates.

NHS patient information on dental abscess describes infection requiring timely professional treatment and emergency contexts such as breathing or swallowing difficulty. Its wisdom-tooth-removal page discusses infection, nerve injury and seeking help for persistent bleeding. These are UK patient resources, not complete guidance for every maxillofacial operation. Record-conflict and follow-up questions are editorial prompts, not clinical management instructions.
Qualified teams responsible for infection assessment, handover and emergency-care coordination
Dental abscess may involve breathing or swallowing difficulty requiring urgent professional care. This page provides no anesthesia or airway-management plan.

This editorial paper exercise checks only the supplied identifiers, versions, sides and missing fields. Retain unknowns and write verification questions. Do not determine disease, surgical indications, anesthesia or readiness for surgery; use no real patients or records. Completion grants no medical qualification.

In the U.S., professional dental education such as a DDS/DMD is generally followed by four to six years of OMS specialty training, sometimes combined with an MD. State licensure, ABOMS board certification and hospital privileges are distinct. For mainland China, check dental education, physician qualification examinations, registration and post requirements separately. Specialty training for existing practitioners is not an initial entry route.
Training and authorization

Complete fictional inputs (v1; not clinical records): K01 has planned side=left, imaging-label side=right, consent side=left; anesthesia-assessment field=not supplied, authorized-review signature field=not supplied. L01 has planned side=right, imaging-label side=right, consent side=right; anesthesia-assessment field=blank, authorized-review signature field=blank. Each identifier agrees across its own records. No images, diagnoses, patient circumstances, actual appointments or professional feedback are supplied. Task: copy each original value, flag side conflicts and missing/unknown fields, and list questions for a qualified team. Do not complete assessments, add signatures or change sides.
Fictional surgical document problem statement

Field-by-field reference (v1): K01 | plan left | imaging label right | consent left | assessment not supplied | signature not supplied. The sides conflict; the correct side cannot be determined, and the two unspecified fields remain unknown. L01 | plan right | imaging label right | consent right | assessment blank | signature blank. Agreement is only a consistency finding; it does not establish completed assessment, authorization for surgery or patient safety. Submit one two-row original-value and flag table. Ask a qualified team to verify K01’s three original documents and unspecified fields, and whether valid records exist elsewhere for L01’s two blank fields. Submit a separate question list and correction-trail note that retains originals and labels personal annotations. No professional response is supplied; do not claim review or clearance occurred.
Text-checking reference and verification questions

Seven-day exploration: Day 1 read the complete K01/L01-v1 inputs and boundaries. Days 2–3 copy the two original rows without changing sides. Days 4–5 use the reference to flag conflicting sides, unspecified fields and blanks, distinguishing unknown from absent. Days 6–7 submit the original-value table, question list and correction-trail note; reflect on your interest in detailed records and team communication. List airway, infection, nerve injury and bleeding as topics to ask about in formal programs and team responsibilities, without inferring clinical risks or decisions from this exercise.

directions.fit_signals: Compare your interest in broad dental care and specialty surgery.
directions.watchouts: General dentists also need professional dental education and licensing; OMS adds specialty surgical training, rather than a simple surgery/no-surgery distinction.

directions.fit_signals: Explore interest in dentofacial correction and longitudinal records.
directions.watchouts: Focuses on jaw relationships and corrective plans; verify specialty training and practice requirements separately.

directions.fit_signals: Compare interest in function, prosthetic design and fitting.
directions.watchouts: Focuses on prostheses, function and fitting; distinguish fabrication collaboration from clinical responsibilities.

directions.fit_signals: Research further if pediatric populations and the relevant medical training interest you.
directions.watchouts: Patient populations, anatomy and pediatric surgical training differ; dental credentials are not pediatric surgical qualifications.

directions.fit_signals: Compare interest in clinical assistance, preparation and records.
directions.watchouts: Limited assisting duties depend on applicable rules and do not grant independent diagnostic or surgical rights.

directions.fit_signals: Compare interest in materials, precise fabrication and specification checks.
directions.watchouts: Focuses on fabrication and device techniques; clinical communication background proves neither fabrication skill nor patient-care authority.
